actions.allocationIsOnlyDuringTheAllocat: Allocation is only during the allocation phase.
actions.allocationPhaseCaptainHasActionP: Allocation phase. Captain has {pool} Action Point{pool2} to distribute for this turn.
actions.antibodiesCanTNeutraliseVenomIt: Antibodies can't neutralise venom — it acts far too fast for your B-cells to respond. You need ANTIVENOM (a dose you have, or one you order).
actions.antivenomDeliveredOneMoreVialIn: Antivenom delivered — one more vial ({antivenom} in stock). Your body cannot make this: it is antibodies raised in horses, and it has to be brought to you. Antivenom shortages are a real and deadly problem in rural India.
actions.antivenomGivenNeutralisedInstant: Antivenom given — {disease} neutralised instantly. These are borrowed antibodies (made in horses): fast, but they do not last and your body learns nothing. {antivenom} dose(s) left.
actions.aPathogenNobodyHasEverSeen: ⚠ A PATHOGEN NOBODY HAS EVER SEEN. Your antibodies do not fit it — not one of them. Your innate cells (Monocyte, Neutrophil, NK) still work and must hold the line, while your B-Cells search millions of receptors for the ONE clone that matches. This is what a new pandemic feels like from inside a body.
actions.aResidentMovesOneStepAt: A resident moves one step at a time.
actions.bCellsSearchingForAMatching: B-Cells searching for a matching clone… {clone}/{CLONECOST}. Your body is sifting millions of random receptors for one that fits.
actions.brandNewAntigenNoAntibodyFits: Brand-new antigen — no antibody fits it yet. Run CLONAL SELECTION first.
actions.cannotReachItInTheBloodstream: Cannot reach it in the bloodstream.
actions.cannotReachItInTheBloodstream2: Cannot reach it in the bloodstream yet.
actions.captainConfirmedThePlanEachPlaye: Captain confirmed the plan. Each player may now spend their allocated Action Points.
actions.changedItsCoatYourAntibodyNo: {disease} changed its coat — your antibody no longer fits. (Antigenic variation: this is why it has no vaccine.)
actions.chooseWhichAntigenClassToMake: Choose which antigen class to make antibodies against.
actions.clonalSelectionCompleteOutOfMill: CLONAL SELECTION COMPLETE. Out of millions of B-cells, you found the ONE whose receptor fits this new antigen — and cloned it. You can now make antibodies against the unknown pathogen. This search is exactly why the first response to a new germ takes days.
actions.coatItWithAnAntibodyFirst: Coat it with an antibody first — cells cannot grip an uncoated parasite.
actions.coatItWithAnAntibodyFirst2: Coat it with an antibody first.
actions.degranulateIsForAWormOr: Degranulate is for a worm or parasite.
actions.degranulateTakes2ActionPointsIt: Degranulate takes 2 Action Points — it's the eosinophil's whole payload.
actions.eosinophilDegranulatedAFullToxic: Eosinophil DEGRANULATED — a full toxic payload for 3 damage (2 AP). {maxhp} The cell is spent and regenerates on turn {regenAt}. This is how eosinophils really kill worms — and why parasites cause tissue damage.
actions.everyInfectionFacedAndTheBody: Every infection faced and the body is completely clear — you win!
actions.itIsHidingInsideLiverCells: It is hiding inside liver cells — antibodies cannot reach it.
actions.itIsHidingInsideYourOwn: It is hiding INSIDE your own macrophage — an antibody cannot get in there.
actions.itIsLivingInsideYourOwn: It is living INSIDE your own macrophage — antibodies cannot reach inside your cells. A Killer T-Cell must activate the infected cell to destroy it.
actions.memoryAntibodiesDestroyedInstant: Memory antibodies destroyed {disease} instantly — no Action Point spent.
actions.memoryResponseDestroyedRecognise: Memory response destroyed {disease} — recognised and cleared at once.{difficulty}
actions.memoryResponseYourBodyHasMet: MEMORY RESPONSE. Your body has met {dz} before, so memory cells recognise it instantly. {costTxt} This is why you only get chickenpox once — and it works only on {dz2}, not on other germs of the same type.
actions.moveTheEosinophilOntoTheTarget: Move the Eosinophil onto the target first.
actions.need1ActionPointForThe: Need 1 Action Point for the memory response on Hard.
actions.neutralisingAToxinTakesActionPoi: Neutralising a toxin takes {apCost} Action Points.
actions.nkCellIsNotInPlay: NK Cell is not in play.
actions.nkCellRolledDestroyedTheInfected: NK Cell rolled {roll} — destroyed the infected cell holding {disease}. Innate: no antigen needed.
actions.nkCellRolledMissedInnateKilling: NK Cell rolled {roll} — missed. Innate killing is fast but imprecise; the Killer T-Cell never misses.
actions.noAntibodiesCanBeMadeThis: No antibodies can be made this turn (immunosuppression).
actions.noInfectedCellWithinNkRange: No infected cell within NK range.
actions.noLymphaticLinkFromThisRoute: No lymphatic link from this route.
actions.nothingHereANetCanCatch: Nothing here a NET can catch — a NET holds living microbes, but toxins and venom are not alive, and worms and protozoa are far too big.
actions.nothingToEngulfWhereItStands: Nothing to engulf where it stands — move it onto a virus or a tagged bacterium first.

actions.onlyTheCaptainEndsTheTurn: Only the captain ends the turn.
actions.onlyTheEosinophil2DamageAnd: Only the Eosinophil (2 damage) and the Monocyte (1 damage) can strike a worm or parasite from the outside — the Neutrophil and NK Cell cannot.
actions.onTrainingImmunityComesFromSurvi: On Training, immunity comes from SURVIVING an infection — beat a disease and your body remembers it. Vaccines come into play on Normal and Hard.
actions.pickADiseaseToDevelopA: Pick a disease to develop a vaccine against.
actions.pickAnUntaggedBacteriumWormOr: Pick an untagged bacterium, worm or parasite.
actions.strikeIsForWormsAndProtozoan: Strike is for worms and protozoan parasites — the EUK targets too big to simply engulf.
actions.theBloodRouteHasNoLymphatic: The Blood route has NO lymphatic link — a needle goes straight into the bloodstream, bypassing the tissues entirely. That is exactly why it is so dangerous.
actions.theCaptainSApIsAlready: The captain's AP is already the unallocated pool.

actions.theLymphaticCrossingIsAtStep: The lymphatic crossing is at step {LYMPHSTEP} of a route.

actions.theNeutrophilIsRegeneratingAndCa: The Neutrophil is regenerating and cannot act yet.

actions.thereIsNoUnknownAntigenTo: There is no unknown antigen to search for.
actions.thisAntigenIsBrandNewNo: This antigen is BRAND NEW — no antibody you own fits it. Run CLONAL SELECTION to find the matching B-cell clone.
actions.thisResidentHasAParasiteLiving: This resident has a parasite living inside it — it can't eat anything until you kill the parasite.
actions.vaccineCompleteYouNowHaveMemory: VACCINE COMPLETE — {dz}. You now have memory cells for it WITHOUT ever having been ill. If it appears, your response will be immediate. This is what a vaccine actually is: memory without the disease.
actions.youAreAlreadyImmuneToThat: You are already immune to that.
actions.youCannotVaccinateAgainstSomethi: You cannot vaccinate against something your body has never seen.
actions.youCanOnlyReturnApDuring: You can only return AP during the allocation phase.

actions.yourAntibodiesDoNotNeutraliseThi: Your antibodies do not neutralise this dengue serotype — they HELP it into your cells (ADE). Use the Monocyte, Neutrophil or NK Cell.

construct.aCoInfectionThreatenedButNothi: A co-infection threatened, but nothing new took hold.

effects.defeatedMemoryCellsForItNow: {disease} defeated. Memory cells for it now survive in your body — if it ever returns, your response will be immediate.
effects.theIsFreeAgainTheParasite: The {RESIDENTNAME} is FREE again — the parasite inside it is dead.{how}
spread.complementCoatedInTheBloodstreamA: Complement coated {disease} in the bloodstream — a phagocyte can now eat it.
spread.crowdedSpotSStoppedGrowingA: {size} crowded spot(s) stopped growing — a single tissue space holds at most {SPACECAP} bacteria. Real bacterial growth is density-limited. Note the cap is per SPOT, so the same disease can still build up on several spots at once.
spread.damagedKidneysLeakedAAntibodyInto: Damaged kidneys leaked a {f} antibody into the urine.
spread.feverHoldsTheInvadersNoAdvance: Fever holds the invaders — no advance this turn.
spread.hasLodgedInYourAWorm: {disease} has lodged in your {name}. A worm does not pass through — it settles in and feeds, chewing the organ a little more every few turns until you kill it. You have a short while before it starts to bite. Coat it, then the Eosinophil strikes — or Degranulates for the kill.
spread.hasMovedInsideYourYourOwn: {disease} has moved INSIDE your {organ}. Your own defender cell is now the parasite's house — it can no longer eat anything. Kill the parasite to free it.
spread.immuneAmnesiaMeaslesHasWipedOut: IMMUNE AMNESIA. Measles has wiped out your immune memory — every antigen you had learned is GONE. Antibody production drops back to the beginning. This really happens.
spread.isNowCirculatingInTheBlood: {disease} is now circulating in the blood. Antibodies and the Monocyte can reach it.
spread.isStillFeedingInYourIntegrity: {disease} is still feeding in your {name} — integrity {hp}/{max}. Kill it to stop the bleeding.
spread.lymphaticSpreadInfectionSTravelle: Lymphatic spread! {length} infection(s) travelled through the lymph system into a neighbouring region. The lymphatics are not only your highway — germs ride them too.
spread.malariaBurstOutOfTheLiver: Malaria burst out of the liver — 3 blood-stage parasites are now in the bloodstream. NOW antibodies work on them.
spread.malariaSlippedInsideYourLiverCell: Malaria slipped inside your liver cells. Antibodies cannot touch it in there — only the Killer T-Cell or the NK Cell can. It will burst out in {MALARIALIVERTURNS} turns.
spread.theBodyCouldNotBeCleared: The body could not be cleared of infection in time — the immune system is exhausted. Defeat.
spread.theIsScarredIntegrityStaysBut: The {name} is scarred (integrity stays {hp}/{max}) but the body has compensated — its penalty no longer applies.
spread.theYouLeftAliveHasStarted: The {disease} you left alive has started releasing {tname}! A toxin is not alive — only antibodies can neutralise it.
spread.virusEsHidInsideACell: {n} virus(es) hid inside a cell — antibodies can no longer touch them. The Killer T-Cell (never misses) or the NK Cell (d6 3+) must kill the infected cell.
